value.name: Marilyn defends Miles
value.description: Marilyn tells the others that Miles is right, backing his position on the cigars.
evidence: MARYLIN You know, sweets, he's right.

value.name: Miles identifies the cigars as pre-Castro
value.description: Miles looks at the cigars ruefully and clarifies that they are pre-Castro Cohibas.
evidence: Miles casts a rueful look at the cigars.

value.name: Marylin worries about Miles's safety
value.description: Pregnant Marylin says the cigars were made under a dictatorship and asks what she would tell their son if Miles died.
evidence: MARYLIN Fine. They were created during a dictatorship.
(Placing a protective hand on her BIG belly) What if something happened to you? What would I tell little Gus when he asked "what was my daddy like?"

value.name: Miles gives cigars to construction worker
value.description: After looking between the cigars and his wife, Miles tosses the box to the concerned construction worker.
evidence: Miles looks at the box, then at his wife. He tosses the box to the concerned construction worker.
MILES Here, buddy. These are for you.

value.name: Construction worker reacts angrily
value.description: The construction worker responds with hostility and jokes that the cigars will kill him.
evidence: The construction worker gives him a very hostile look.
CONSTRUCTION WORKER (Mumbles) Great. Now I can die.

value.name: Miles jokes about his legacy
value.description: Miles responds with a self-deprecating joke about his reputation and Marylin's role in his life.
evidence: MILES Well. You'd say "they devoted a whole semester at Harvard to your Dad. But your Mom was the one that ever only nailed his ass."
